name: Unfractionated heparin
executiveSummary: UFH. ACS/DVT: bolus **60–80 IU/kg** (usual max **4000–5000 IU**) then **12–18 IU/kg/h** IV titrated to aPTT/anti-Xa. SC prophylaxis: **5000 IU q8–12h**. Antidote: **protamine**. HIT risk — monitor platelets.
indications:
## Indications

- Treatment/prophylaxis of thromboembolism; ACS; cardiopulmonary bypass; perioperative bridge.

## Precautions

- Bleeding; HIT type II (stop and do not use LMWH if HIT).
- aPTT q6h until stable. Adjust in obesity/CKD per protocol.
- Not IM. Neuraxial anesthesia: strict safety windows.

> Prefer LMWH in many ambulatory settings; UFH if imminent surgery or severe CKD.

adulto.dose: IV treatment: bolus **80 IU/kg** (or **60** in ACS) → infusion **18 IU/kg/h** (ACS often **12 IU/kg/h**) titrated. Prophylaxis: **5000 IU SC q8–12h**. Line flushes: local concentrations (e.g. 10–100 IU/mL) — not therapeutic.
adulto.administration: IV pump / SC abdomen. Never IM.
adulto.notes: Protamine: ~1 mg per 100 IU UFH in last 2–3 h (usual initial max ~50 mg).

pediatrico.dose: Bolus **75 IU/kg** → **20–28 IU/kg/h** (younger/neonates higher per kg) — protocol + anti-Xa/aPTT.

neonatal.dose: NICU schemes (bolus ~75 IU/kg; infusion ~28 IU/kg/h) — protocol only.

stability:
## Stability

- Infusion in NS/D5W per compatibility; prepare extemporaneously.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bleeding, hematoma, HIT, osteoporosis (chronic), alopecia, hyperkalemia.
